question: Which railway safety system did India begin implementing nationwide, covering 3,500 km in 2025 at a cost of ₹1,700 crore?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kavach Automatic Train Protection**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kavach Automatic Train Protection (ATP)** is an **indigenous railway safety system** developed by the Indian Railways to enhance train safety and prevent accidents such as collisions and derailments.
 
• The implementation of the **Kavach system** is a significant milestone in the Indian Railways' efforts to modernize its infrastructure and improve safety. By **2025**, the system is planned to cover a distance of **3,500 km** at a cost of **₹1,700 crore**.
 
• The Kavach system uses **state-of-the-art technologies** like signals passed at danger (SPAD), automatic braking in case of driver error, and real-time communication between the train and signaling systems to ensure the highest level of safety.
 
• It was successfully tested on **March 4, 2022**, with a demonstration attended by the **Union Minister of Railways, Ashwini Vaishnaw**, showcasing its effectiveness in preventing accidents.
 
• The Indian government aims to expand the Kavach system to cover the entire railway network, ensuring the safety of passengers and reducing risks associated with human errors in train operations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Features of Kavach System:**

 
 
• **Automatic Braking:** The Kavach system automatically applies brakes to prevent collisions in case the train overshoots a signal or encounters another train on the same track.
 
• **SPAD (Signals Passed at Danger):** It ensures that the train halts before passing a danger signal, thereby averting potential accidents.
 
• **Real-Time Communication:** The system allows real-time communication between trains and station signaling systems to provide updates on movement and track conditions.
 
• **Indigenous Development:** Kavach is a **Make in India initiative**, developed by Indian Railways, which ensures cost-effectiveness and promotes local manufacturing capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Kavach:**
 
 
• It aims to reduce human errors, which are a leading cause of train accidents in India.
 
• Kavach is expected to significantly enhance passenger safety and improve the efficiency of train operations on Indian railways.
 
• As part of the modernization drive, the Indian Railways plans to implement this system across its high-density routes and ensure safer and faster travel for passengers.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Options:**
 
 
• **Nationwide Railway Safety System:** This is a generic term and does not refer to any specific system implemented by Indian Railways.
 
• **Namo Bharat Signalling System:** No such system exists in Indian Railways under this name.
 
• **GPS-based Tracking System:** While GPS technology is used for tracking trains, it is not a comprehensive safety system like Kavach, which includes automatic braking and SPAD features.
 
 
 
• **Future Plans:**
 
 
• The Indian Railways has set a target to implement the Kavach system across **34,000 km of its network**, focusing on high-density routes.
 
• The initiative aligns with the government's vision of achieving high levels of safety and reliability in the railway sector.
